title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story
gist: Summary of McKinsey's September 2026 analysis raising its 2030 semiconductor market base case to $2.3T (from $1.6T in autumn 2025; range $1.7T-$2.6T), driven by data-center chip revenue rising from $330B (2025) to $1.2T (2030), with leading-edge logic (+$710B) and memory/HBM (+$560B) capturing gains while mature nodes see price declines.

insights.claim: McKinsey raised its 2030 base-case semiconductor market forecast to $2.3 trillion in September 2026, up from $1.6 trillion projected in autumn 2025.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A ~44% upward revision in one year signals consultants/strategists are chasing AI demand; supports capex plans across foundry, memory and equipment.

insights.claim: McKinsey's 2030 semiconductor market scenarios range from $1.7 trillion to $2.6 trillion, so even the bear case exceeds its prior $1.6 trillion base case.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The floor of the new range is above the old base case, implying a structural reset in expectations rather than a marginal tweak.

insights.claim: McKinsey attributes the forecast revision to an exceptional surge in chip sales driven by AI, which is changing both the size of the semiconductor market and where its profits are made.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Profit-pool shift matters more than total size: position toward the segments capturing AI value.

insights.claim: McKinsey expects semiconductor revenue from servers and data centers to rise from $330 billion in 2025 to $1.2 trillion in 2030, roughly 3.6x in five years.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Data-center exposure (AI accelerators, HBM, networking) is where the bulk of incremental semiconductor revenue is forecast to land.
insights.locator: Data centers drive much of the

insights.claim: Demand is rising especially for leading-edge processors and high-bandwidth memory (HBM), which keeps AI computing hardware supplied with data.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Supports continued strength for HBM suppliers and leading-edge foundry capacity.
insights.locator: Data centers drive much of the

insights.claim: Because leading-edge and memory manufacturing capacity is constrained, McKinsey expects both volumes and average selling prices to rise in these segments, breaking the industry's usual pattern of falling prices as production expands.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Rising ASPs plus volume imply margin expansion for capacity-constrained suppliers; watch for capacity additions that could end the pricing regime.
insights.quote: That combination differs from the industry’s familiar pattern of falling prices as production expands.
insights.locator: Data centers drive much of the

insights.claim: Mature/older manufacturing nodes will keep supplying connectivity, power and other components, but with smaller growth and declining prices even as volumes rise.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Bifurcated market: underweight mature-node pure plays relative to leading-edge and memory exposure.

insights.claim: McKinsey estimates leading-edge chips could add $710 billion in market value by 2030.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Largest single incremental pool; benefits leading-edge foundries and advanced-node designers.

insights.claim: McKinsey estimates memory could add another $560 billion in market value by 2030.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Memory is nearly as large an incremental pool as leading-edge logic, supporting a structural (not only cyclical) memory thesis.

insights.claim: The $2.3 trillion outcome depends on sustained data-center funding, measurable AI returns, affordable power, lower AI inference costs and a stable economy.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Use these five conditions as a monitoring checklist for the AI-semis trade (hyperscaler capex, AI ROI, power prices, inference cost curves, macro).

insights.claim: A recession, trade disruption or disappointing AI returns could weaken semiconductor investment and push outcomes toward the low end of the range.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Downside scenario ($1.7T) is the relevant stress case; tariff/export-control news and AI ROI data are key swing factors.

insights.claim: McKinsey advises chipmakers to prepare for a much larger market while stress-testing investments against multiple scenarios, treating the forecast as both opportunity and planning challenge.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Expect capex guidance with scenario hedging (phased fabs, flexible capacity) rather than all-in commitments.
